newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T. Industries reports cigarette sales growth.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T. Industries reports cigarette sales growth.

text.p: Tobacco to insurance group B.A.T Industries Plc reported a strong 10 percent growth in sales of its international filter brands on Wednesday, selling more than 40 billion cigarettes in the first quarter.
International brands include State Express 555, Kent and Benson and Hedges outside Europe.

"One of the trends around the world is for people to trade up to international brands. The biggest growth in international is coming from the Far East. Japan is definitely a success story," said Michael Prideaux, director of public affairs.
Total group cigarette sales rose only slightly however to 167 billion, held back by lower sales in North America.

Tobacco profit from the America-Pacific region was lower at 140 million pounds ($228 million) in the first quarter. Reduced sales in a very competitive U.S. domestic market and the loss of contribution from the consent order brands sold at the end of 1996, more than offset the benefit of last year's price increase.
B.A.T's American subsidiary Brown & Williamson saw lower shipments and its market share fell to 16.3 percent from 17.5 percent, mainly due to the sale of the consent order brands.
But the import sector in Japan increased and the group's total market rose to 5.9 percent with further progress from Kent, Lucky Strike, Kool and Capri.

B.A.T's tobacco profits from the Asia-Pacific region were 15 percent higher at 88 million sterling after greater marketing investment. Profits were higher in Australia and Indonesia and in Latin America higher prices and lower costs pushed the group's tobacco profits to 65 million sterling. ($ = 0.614 British Pounds)
